assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (bill/casque) but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en: The hornbill's big strong bill has a horn-like bump on top called a casque.
copy.tl: Ang tuka ng kalaw ay malaki at matibay, may parang sungay na bukol sa ibabaw na tinatawag na casque.
copy.bis: Ang tuka sa kalaw dako ug lig-on, adunay morag sungay nga bukol sa ibabaw nga gitawag og casque.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the kalaw 'calls' instead of sings
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a living thing's vocalization but does not address the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its loud honk or cackle sends a message
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound sending a message, but the competency specifically requires using movement, sound, or light to send information between two people. The card describes animal communication, not human-to-human information transfer, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its loud honk or cackle sends a message
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a sound made by an animal but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It only states that the kalaw makes a loud call, without explaining sound production or transfer, so it is only related to the topic of sound.

copy.en:
Does the kalaw really sing?

Not really — the kalaw 'calls' instead of sings. Its loud honk or cackle sends a message; it isn't a melodic song like a sparrow's.
copy.tl:
Kumakanta ba talaga ang kalaw?

Hindi pala — 'tumatawag' ang kalaw imbes na umawit. Malakas na honk o tawa ang tunog nito para magpadala ng mensahe, hindi para sa ganda ng himig.
copy.bis:
Mokanta ba gyud ang kalaw?

Dili diay — 'motawag' ang kalaw imbes nga moawit. Kusog nga honk o katawa ang tingog niini aron magpadala og mensahe, dili para sa kanindot sa tunog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That skin has no feathers on it, so the color of the blood underneath shows through
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: A bare eye patch is not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the color of the blood underneath shows through — making it look red or pink
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Blood showing through skin is color, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
Why does a kalaw's eye patch look reddish?

That skin has no feathers on it, so the color of the blood underneath shows through — making it look red or pink!
copy.tl:
Bakit mapula ang balat sa paligid ng mata ng kalaw?

Dahil hubad sa balahibo ang balat doon, kaya kita mo ang kulay ng dugo sa ilalim nito — kaya mukhang pula o pink!
copy.bis:
Ngano pula ang panit palibot sa mata sa kalaw?

Tungod kay walay balhibo ang panit didto, mao nga makita ang kolor sa dugo sa ilawom — mao nga morag pula o pink!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: with vivid red and yellow on its face and bill
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the face and bill (outer body parts) but does not describe their role in movement or food gathering, which is the core of G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tarictic is a smaller Philippine hornbill with a less red face
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares two bird species but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (e.g., birds, mammals, etc.), so it does not directly support G5-L-4.

copy.en: The tarictic is a smaller Philippine hornbill with a less red face — but the kalaw is the biggest, with vivid red and yellow on its face and bill!
copy.tl: Ang tarictic ay mas maliit na hornbill sa Pilipinas na hindi gaanong mapula ang mukha — pero ang kalaw ang pinakamalaki, may matingkad na pula at dilaw sa mukha at tuka!
copy.bis: Ang tarictic mas gamay nga hornbill sa Pilipinas nga dili kaayo pula ang nawong — apan ang kalaw mao ang pinakadako, adunay tin-aw nga pula ug dalag sa nawong ug sungo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its young leaves and tops are also a nutritious vegetable.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves and roots but only as edible parts, not their role in absorbing water and nutrients from the soil. It does not support the competency's focus on plant part functions.

copy.en: It's not just the kamote root that's eaten — its young leaves and tops are also a nutritious vegetable.
copy.tl: Hindi lang ang ugat ng kamote ang kinakain — ang mga dahon o talbos nito ay masustansyang gulay din.
copy.bis: Dili lang ang gamot sa kamote ang gikaon — ang mga dahon o talbos niini usa usab ka masustansyang utanon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: potato is a swollen underground stem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies potato as a swollen underground stem (a tuber) and kamote as a root, but it does not describe the purpose or function of these specialized structures. The competency requires describing the purpose of specialized structures such as tubers and roots, which the card does not address.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Kamote is actually a root, but potato is a swollen underground stem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots and stems as plant parts, but it does not describe their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. The competency focuses on observing outer parts and identifying their function in water/nutrient uptake, which is not covered.

copy.en:
Are kamote and potato the same plant?

No! Kamote is actually a root, but potato is a swollen underground stem — two very different plants.
copy.tl:
Magkatulad ba ang kamote at patatas?

Hindi pala! Ang kamote ay ugat, pero ang patatas ay namamagang tangkay sa ilalim ng lupa — magkaibang halaman.
copy.bis:
Managsama ba ang kamote ug patatas?

Dili diay! Ang kamote usa ka gamot, apan ang patatas usa ka namaga nga lawas ilalom sa yuta — lahi nga mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A kangaroo has a pouch on its belly where its baby, called a joey, lives, grows, and drinks milk!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a kangaroo's pouch and joey but does not identify which groups of animals give birth to live young versus lay eggs. It does not mention mammals, birds, reptiles, or the contrast between live birth and egg-laying, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A kangaroo has a pouch on its belly where its baby, called a joey, lives, grows, and drinks milk!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a joey growing in a pouch but does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants. It does not address stages from birth to adulthood or egg to mature organism, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What is a baby kangaroo called?

A kangaroo has a pouch on its belly where its baby, called a joey, lives, grows, and drinks milk!
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa sanggol ng kangaroo?

Ang kangaroo ay may bulsa sa tiyan kung saan nakatira at lumalaki ang sanggol nito, ang tinatawag na joey, habang sumususo ng gatas!
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa gamay nga kangaroo?

Ang kangaroo adunay puyo sa tiyan diin nagpuyo ug nagtubo ang iyang gamay, ang gitawag og joey, samtang nagsuso og gatas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The soft fibers from the kapok tree are used to stuff pillows and mattresses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant product (kapok fibers) but does not address observing outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water/nutrient uptake. It shares only the broad topic of plants.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The soft fibers from the kapok tree are used to stuff pillows and mattresses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not discuss the root or shoot system of plants or their importance. It only mentions a use of kapok fibers, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on plant systems.

copy.en: The soft fibers from the kapok tree are used to stuff pillows and mattresses.
copy.tl: Ang malambot na hibla ng kapok ay ginagamit na palaman sa mga unan at kutson.
copy.bis: Ang humok nga lanot sa kapok gigamit nga sulod sa mga unlan ug kutson.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a kapok pod ripens, it splits open and soft, fluffy fiber spills out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: A splitting pod spilling fiber is fruit anatomy, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

copy.en: When a kapok pod ripens, it splits open and soft, fluffy fiber spills out.
copy.tl: Kapag hinog na ang bunga ng kapok, pumipitik ito at lumalabas ang malambot na hibla.
copy.bis: Kon hinog na ang bunga sa kapok, mobuka kini ug mogawas ang humok nga lanot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: ground peanuts mix into the water to form a thick mixture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of a mixture (peanuts in water) but does not describe it as uniform or non-uniform, nor as a solution or suspension. It does not directly support the competency's requirement to describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures.

copy.en: Kare-kare's sauce thickens as it cooks because ground peanuts mix into the water to form a thick mixture!
copy.tl: Lumalapot ang sarsa ng kare-kare habang niluluto dahil ang giniling na mani ay naghahalo sa tubig para maging makapal!
copy.bis: Molapot ang sarsa sa kare-kare samtang gilutoan kay ang giniling nga mani mosagol sa tubig aron mahimong baga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A landscape called karst forms when limestone dissolves, creating caves, sinkholes, and hills!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes karst formation by dissolution of limestone, which is chemical weathering, not the transport of Earth materials by erosion. It does not demonstrate how erosion transports materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A landscape called karst forms when limestone dissolves, creating caves, sinkholes, and hills!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a landform (karst) but does not identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, nor does it describe how they influence living and non-living components. It only gives a general definition of karst.

copy.en: A landscape called karst forms when limestone dissolves, creating caves, sinkholes, and hills!
copy.tl: Ang tanawin na tinatawag na karst ay nabubuo kapag natutunaw ang limestone, na lumilikha ng mga kweba, sinkhole, at burol!
copy.bis: Ang talan-awon nga gitawag karst maporma kung matunaw ang limestone, nga maghimo og mga langob, sinkhole, ug bungtod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: piled-up sea shells, coral, and tiny animal skeletons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fossil-like materials (shells, coral, skeletons) as components of limestone, but does not describe how fossils are used for dating the age of rocks and sediments. No dating concept is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: limestone that shapes karst landscapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a type of rock (limestone) but does not involve exploring, collecting, or comparing rocks by texture, color, or grain crystal size. It only states a fact about limestone's origin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: millions of years of piled-up sea shells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a long time span (millions of years) but does not explain the geologic time scale or how it recounts Earth's history. No time-scale framework is presented.

copy.en:
What is limestone actually made of?

The limestone that shapes karst landscapes comes from millions of years of piled-up sea shells, coral, and tiny animal skeletons that slowly hardened into solid rock!
copy.tl:
Ano ba talaga ang gawa ng batong-apog?

Ang batong-apog na hinuhubog sa karst ay galing sa milyon-milyong taong naipong kabibe, coral, at buto ng maliliit na hayop sa dagat na tumigas at naging bato!
copy.bis:
Unsa man gyud ang gihimo sa anapog?

Ang anapog nga gikulit sa karst naggikan sa minilyon ka tuig nga natipon nga kabibe, coral, ug bukog sa gagmayng mananap sa dagat nga mitig-a ug nahimong bato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tall, steep limestone hills called tower karst
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines tower karst as a landform but does not identify local examples or describe how landforms influence living and non-living components, which are the core actions of G5-E-1.

copy.en: Some karst form tall, steep limestone hills called tower karst — they stay standing after the surrounding rock dissolves away!
copy.tl: May karst na nagbubuo ng matataas at matatarik na burol na tinatawag na tower karst — nananatili silang nakatayo matapos matunaw ang paligid!
copy.bis: Adunay karst nga naghimo ug habog ug tarik nga bungtod nga gitawag ug tower karst — nagpabilin silang nagtindog human matunaw ang palibot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The katydid got its name from its song
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the origin of the katydid's name based on the sound of its song, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred, which is the focus of G3-F-4. The mention of a song is only a tangential connection to sound.

copy.en:
Why is the katydid named that?

The katydid got its name from its song, which sounds like it's singing 'katy-did, katy-did'!
copy.tl:
Bakit tinawag na katydid ang insektong ito?

Pinangalanan ang katydid batay sa tunog ng kanyang awit na parang sinasabing 'katy-did, katy-did'!
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag og katydid kini nga insekto?

Ginganlan ang katydid base sa tingog sa iyang awit nga morag nag-ingon og 'katy-did, katy-did'!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absolute zero is super cold? It equals about -273 degrees Celsius
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the numeric value of absolute zero in Celsius. It does not describe particle motion, spacing, attraction, or the effect of temperature on particle speed, which are the core of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absolute zero is super cold? It equals about -273 degrees Celsius
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a temperature value but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It provides no instructional support for distinguishing these concepts.

copy.en: Did you know absolute zero is super cold? It equals about -273 degrees Celsius (-273.15°C)!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na super lamig ng absolute zero? Ito ay katumbas ng halos -273 degrees Celsius (-273.15°C)!
copy.bis: Nahibalo ba ka nga super bugnaw ang absolute zero? Kini katumbas sa mga -273 degrees Celsius (-273.15°C)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water freezes at about 273.15 K, which is equal to 0 °C!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on identifying and using units in simple science activities, with examples like mg, g, kg, and degrees centigrade. The card is about the Kelvin temperature of water's freezing point and its Celsius equivalent. It does not teach unit identification or use in a science activity, and Kelvin is not among the listed units. The mention of 0 °C is incidental, not instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
At what temperature does water freeze on the Kelvin scale?

Water freezes at about 273.15 K, which is equal to 0 °C!
copy.tl:
Sa anong temperatura nagyeyelo ang tubig sa Kelvin scale?

Nagyeyelo ang tubig sa mga 273.15 K, na katumbas ng 0 °C!
copy.bis:
Sa unsang temperatura mohahi ang tubig sa Kelvin scale?

Mohahi ang tubig sa mga 273.15 K, nga katumbas sa 0 °C!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: making the solid white curds separate from the watery liquid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions separation of curds from liquid but does not demonstrate or teach any specific separation technique such as filtering, decantation, or sieving. It only describes a natural separation during curdling, not a technique from the competency list.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: curdling carabao's milk with acid or a special enzyme
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: Curdling is a chemical change, but the card does not explain why physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are irreversible. It provides an example of a chemical change without addressing the reversibility concept, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: curdling carabao's milk with acid or a special enzyme
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the indicators for a chemical reaction as color change, the formation of a precipitate, the release of gas, and or odor, or a change in temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes curdling but does not mention any indicator of a chemical reaction such as color change, precipitate formation, gas release, odor, or temperature change. The formation of curds could be seen as a precipitate, but the card does not frame it as an indicator or teach the concept.

copy.en:
How is kesong puti made?

It's made by curdling carabao's milk with acid or a special enzyme, making the solid white curds separate from the watery liquid!
copy.tl:
Paano ginagawa ang kesong puti?

Ginagawa ito sa pamamagitan ng pag-curdle sa gatas ng kalabaw gamit ang acid o special enzyme, na naghihiwalay sa solid white curds!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo ang kesong puti?

Gihimo kini pinaagi sa pag-curdle sa gatas sa kalabaw gamit ang acid o special enzyme, nga nagbulag sa solid white curds!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even a tiny bee or starfish can be a keystone species if it has a big effect on its home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: A tiny keystone species is not competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even a tiny bee or starfish can be a keystone species if it has a big effect on its home
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Keystone size is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
Is the biggest animal always the keystone species?

Nope! Even a tiny bee or starfish can be a keystone species if it has a big effect on its home.
copy.tl:
Ang pinakamalaking hayop ba ang laging keystone?

Hindi pala! Kahit maliit na pukyutan o starfish ay maaaring keystone kung malaki ang epekto nito sa tirahan nito.
copy.bis:
Ang labing dako nga hayop ba kanunay keystone?

Dili diay! Bisan gamay nga putyukan o starfish mahimong keystone kung dako ang epekto niini sa iyang puy-anan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: remove it, and the whole ecosystem can change dramatically
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: remove it, and the whole ecosystem can change dramatically
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: A keystone definition is not explaining how an interaction brings good or harm.

copy.en:
What is a keystone species?

A keystone species has a huge effect on its ecosystem despite being few in number — remove it, and the whole ecosystem can change dramatically.
copy.tl:
Ano ang keystone species?

Ang keystone species ay malaki ang epekto sa ekosistema kahit kakaunti lang sila — kapag inalis ito, biglang magbabago ang buong ekosistema.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang keystone species?

Ang keystone species dako ug epekto sa ekosistema bisan gamay ra sila — kung tangtangon kini, kalit mausab ang tibuok ekosistema.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an umbrella species needs a big area so protecting it protects others too
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not the advantage of high biodiversity during food shortages, disease, or climate change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a keystone holds the whole balance together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: Umbrella, indicator, and keystone species each play a different role: an umbrella species needs a big area so protecting it protects others too, an indicator species shows how healthy the environment is, and a keystone holds the whole balance together.
copy.tl: Magkaiba ang tatlong species na ito: kailangan ng umbrella species ng malawak na lupain kaya napoprotektahan din ang iba, ipinapakita ng indicator species ang kalusugan ng kapaligiran, at hinahawakan ng keystone ang balanse.
copy.bis: Lahi ang tulo ka species: nagkinahanglan ang umbrella species og dako nga luna mao nga naprotektahan usab ang uban, gipakita sa indicator species ang kahimsog sa palibot, ug gikupot sa keystone ang balanse.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the location of the kidneys. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). Kidney location is only loosely related to excretion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You have two bean-shaped kidneys tucked at the back of your belly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: G4-L-1 covers the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The kidneys belong to the excretory/urinary system, which is not among the listed systems, and the card gives no information about how any of the listed systems work.

copy.en: You have two bean-shaped kidneys tucked at the back of your belly, one on each side of your spine.
copy.tl: May dalawang kidney na hugis-bato ang tao, matatagpuan sa likod ng tiyan, isa sa bawat gilid ng gulugod.
copy.bis: Adunay duha ka kidney nga hugis-bato ang tawo, nahimutang sa likod sa tiyan, usa sa matag kilid sa gulugod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Millions of tiny filters called nephrons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about nephrons as kidney filters. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The content is only tangentially related to the excretion system.

copy.en:
What really filters inside your kidney?

Millions of tiny filters called nephrons! They do the real work of sorting water from waste inside each kidney.
copy.tl:
Ano ang talagang nagsasala sa loob ng bato?

Milyun-milyong maliliit na filter na tinatawag na nephron! Sila ang gumagawa ng totoong trabaho ng pagsala ng tubig at dumi sa loob ng bawat bato.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyud ang nagsala sulod sa kidney?

Minilyon ka gagmay nga filter nga gitawag og nephron! Sila ang naghimo sa tinuod nga trabaho sa pagsala sa tubig ug hugaw sulod sa matag kidney.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All of your body's blood flows through the kidneys again and again all day long, keeping it clean
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations of digestion and excretion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All of your body's blood flows through the kidneys again and again all day long, keeping it clean

May tatlong uri ng selula sa mata na sensitibo sa pula, berde, at asul, kaya tatlo lang ang pangunahing kulay ng liwanag!

Adunay tulo ka klase nga selula sa mata nga sensitibo sa pula, berde, ug asul, mao nga tulo lang ang nag-unang kolor sa kahayag!

Bumabagal ang light kapag pumasok ito sa tubig o salamin, at ang pagbabago ng speed na ito ang nagpapaliko nito!

On a stage, when red, green, and blue spotlights overlap, they can make white and many other colors!

Sa entablado, kon magtapok ang pula, berde, ug asul nga mga suga, makahimo sila ug puti ug daghang lain nga kolor!

Paano natin mapipigilan ang matataas na muwebles na matumba sa panahon ng lindol?

Ikabit ang matataas na aparador at estante sa pader! Para hindi ito matumba at makasakit ng iba.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpugong sa mga taas nga muwebles nga matumba panahon sa linog?

Isumpay ang taas nga aparador ug estante sa pader! Aron dili kini matumba ug makasakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A lion in the wild usually lives to be about 10 to 14 years old
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single lifespan fact, not a flow chart comparing life-cycle stages. It does not support the required format or the skill of comparing stages.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A lion in the wild usually lives to be about 10 to 14 years old
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a mammal's lifespan but does not compare life cycles from birth to adulthood or contrast mammals, birds, and plants. It is only tangentially related to life cycles.

copy.en: A lion in the wild usually lives to be about 10 to 14 years old — a fairly short lifespan for such a strong, powerful animal.
copy.tl: Ang isang leon sa kagubatan ay karaniwang nabubuhay lamang ng mga 10 hanggang 14 taon — medyo maikli para sa isang malakas na hayop.
copy.bis: Ang leon sa kalasangan kasagaran mabuhi lang og mga 10 ngadto sa 14 ka tuig — medyo mubo alang sa usa ka kusgan nga mananap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Liquids and gases both flow and move from place to place. Because of this, both are called fluids!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes flow/fluidity of liquids and gases, but G5-M-3 specifically requires describing properties in terms of shape and volume (definite/indefinite). No mention of shape or volume, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Liquids and gases both flow and move from place to place. Because of this, both are called fluids!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions only liquids and gases and a shared property; it does not identify the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases) or state that matter exists in three states. It is related vocabulary but not direct support.

copy.en: Liquids and gases both flow and move from place to place. Because of this, both are called fluids!
copy.tl: Parehong umaagos at gumagalaw ang likido at gas mula sa isang lugar papunta sa iba. Kaya pareho silang tinatawag na fluid!
copy.bis: Parehong modagayday ug mobalhin ang likido ug gas gikan sa usa ka dapit ngadto sa lain. Mao nga pareho silang gitawag nga fluid!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The short abbreviation for the word liter is simply the letter "L"!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only teaches the abbreviation 'L' for liter. It does not address using measuring cylinders or beakers, measuring volume, or the milliliter unit. Knowing the abbreviation is useful background for using the unit, but it does not directly support the measurement skill described in the competency.

copy.en:
How do we write "liter" in short?

Did you know? The short abbreviation for the word liter is simply the letter "L"!
copy.tl:
Paano natin isusulat ang "litro" nang maikli?

Alam mo ba? Ang maikling daglat para sa salitang litro ay ang letrang "L"!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsulat sa "litro" nga mubu?

Nahibaw-an ba nimo? Ang mubo nga daglat para sa pulong litro kay ang letrang "L"!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the body can still stay healthy even if only one is working
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a person can remain healthy with one kidney. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion. The kidney mention is only loosely related to excretion.

copy.en:
Can you live with just one kidney?

Yes — people usually have two kidneys, but the body can still stay healthy even if only one is working.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang mabuhay sa isang bato lang?

Oo — karaniwang may dalawang bato ang tao, pero kaya pa ring mabuhay nang malusog kahit isa na lang ang gumagana.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang mabuhi og usa ra ka kidney?

Oo — kasagaran duha ka kidney ang tawo, apan mahimo pa gihapon mabuhi nga himsog bisan usa ra ang molihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's the liver! It is the largest internal organ inside the human body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the liver being the largest internal organ, but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It shares the human-body topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What's the biggest organ inside your body?

It's the liver! It is the largest internal organ inside the human body.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking organ sa loob ng katawan?

Ang atay! Ito ang pinakamalaking organ sa loob ng katawan ng tao.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga organ sa sulod sa lawas?

Ang atay! Kini mao ang pinakadako nga organ sa sulod sa lawas sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your liver makes bile, a fluid that helps break down the fat in the food you eat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bile, a digestive secretion, but does not use a labeled diagram to trace food through the digestive tract or explain the digestive processes (mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination) as required by the competency. It only provides a single fact about bile's role in fat breakdown, which is related background but not direct support for the competency's specific activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your liver makes bile, a fluid that helps break down the fat in the food you eat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bile, which is part of the digestive system, but does not identify the parts (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) from pictures or labeled diagrams, nor describe how they work. The liver and bile are not among the listed parts, and the card does not support the identification or description of the required digestive organs.

copy.en: Your liver makes bile, a fluid that helps break down the fat in the food you eat.
copy.tl: Gumagawa ang atay ng apdo, isang likidong tumutulong durugin ang taba sa pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang atay naghimo og apdo, usa ka likido nga motabang sa pagdugmok sa tambok sa pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its liver is one of the organs making its blood. After birth, the bone marrow takes over
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Fetal blood-making organs are not the five body systems as a set.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its liver is one of the organs making its blood. After birth, the bone marrow takes over that job
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Where blood is made before birth is origin, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en: Before a baby is even born, while still inside the mother, its liver is one of the organs making its blood. After birth, the bone marrow takes over that job.
copy.tl: Bago pa ipanganak ang isang sanggol, habang nasa tiyan ng ina, ang atay niya ang isa sa gumagawa ng dugo. Pagkasilang, ang bone marrow na ang humahalili sa trabahong ito.
copy.bis: Sa dili pa matawo ang usa ka masuso, samtang naa pa sa sabakan sa inahan, ang iyang atay maoy usa sa naghimo sa dugo. Human matawo, ang bone marrow na ang mopuli sa maong trabaho.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The liver is the largest solid organ in the body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a fact about the liver's size, location, and weight. It does not describe how any body system works, including the digestive system, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The liver is the largest solid organ in the body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together. It merely gives an anatomical fact about the liver.

copy.en: The liver is the largest solid organ in the body — it sits under the ribs on the right side and weighs more than the heart or a kidney.
copy.tl: Ang atay ang pinakamalaking solidong organ sa katawan — nasa ilalim ito ng tadyang sa kanang bahagi, at mas mabigat pa sa puso o bato.
copy.bis: Ang atay mao ang pinakadako nga solido nga organo sa lawas — naa kini ilawom sa gusok sa tuong bahin, ug mas bug-at pa kaysa kasingkasing o kidni.
